intro: Eight questions, about three minutes. This suggests a starting point — it is not a verdict, and switching later costs you much less than you'd think (see the pivot map).

questions.prompt: Which of these sounds most like a good day at work?

options.label: Fixing things people are frustrated about, one after another
Building something from nothing and seeing it work
Digging into numbers until the answer falls out
Making sure a messy operation runs on time

questions.prompt: Be honest about detail. Which is more you?

options.label: I notice the one thing that's wrong in a room of things that are fine
I see the big picture and who needs to talk to whom
I want to understand how the machine actually works underneath
I notice when something is confusing or badly laid out

questions.prompt: How much do you want to write code?

options.label: A lot — that's the point
Some, if it automates boring work
A little — queries and scripts are fine
Ideally none

questions.prompt: How soon do you need to be earning from this?

options.label: As fast as possible — under 6 months
Within about a year
I can take 1–2 years if the ceiling is higher

questions.prompt: Do you have regular access to a computer you can install things on?

options.label: No — phone only right now
Sometimes — library or a shared computer
Yes, my own machine

questions.prompt: What's your realistic study budget over the next year?

options.label: Essentially $0 — free only
A few hundred dollars if it's clearly worth it
$1,000+ across the year

questions.prompt: How do you feel about being on the phone or in meetings with people?

options.label: Fine — I'm good with people, that's my strength
I can do it, but I'd rather focus on the work
I'd like as little of it as possible

questions.prompt: Which of these have you already done, even outside tech? (Pick all that apply.)

options.label: Trained or supervised other people
Built spreadsheets people actually relied on
Fixed computers, phones, or networks for friends and family
Made something visual — flyers, layouts, photo editing
Written any code at all, even a little
Caught mistakes others missed — counts, orders, paperwork

noPc.note: You marked phone-only access. Paths whose early steps need your own machine are ranked lower here, and the Library view lists every step you can start without one.

sharedPc.note: Library or shared computer access works for a surprising amount of this — especially browser-based learning.

freeOnly.note: You marked a $0 budget. Paths with mandatory paid certifications are ranked lower — but note that CompTIA vouchers can often be funded through workforce grants, and Coursera financial aid is routinely approved.
